parts.note: a nation ruled through its police, read as one whose 'force' (the police) governs it

explanation.surface: A question about which nation has a strong ruling power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' is the usual British term for a police service, so the governing force is the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime controlling citizens through police surveillance and repression is the textbook totalitarian nation.

parts.note: ova are eggs, in the Latin plural

explanation.surface: Some eggs have been dropped and left lying on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground, home of Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oval in Kennington is a famous cricket venue, so it is a sports field named by its stadium.

clue.text: Having arrived I run round during the anthem

parts.note: someone who has arrived is in

indicators.note: the word for running goes round the letter I, enclosing it

parts.note: to trot is to run at a gentle pace

explanation.surface: Someone turns up just as the choir is singing and jogs around the church.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a national anthem; the definition is a church chant. 'during the' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An introit is the psalm or chant sung at the start of Mass, a piece of church music like an anthem.

clue.text: Man losing his way gets the bird

indicators.note: the man's name drops the letters for the road, as if losing its way

parts.note: Ernest is a man's name
ST, short for street, is a way

explanation.surface: A man who loses his way ends up with a bird instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes ST from ERNEST, leaving the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the white-tailed sea eagle, a crossword favourite among birds.

indicators.note: dithering is nervous wavering, signalling that the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An indecisive merchant admits to holding things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dithering' rearranges TRADER and I.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarry is to linger, so tarried means stayed behind or was late.

clue.text: It could be instrumental in lifting plunder

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting the word for plunder makes it read upwards, backwards

parts.note: loot is plunder

explanation.surface: Something was a key factor in a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'lifting' reverses LOOT; 'lifting' also suggests stealing in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool is an implement, something that serves as an instrument or means.

indicators.note: an arrangement of the letters puts them in a new order

explanation.surface: Office workers complain that the seating plan is all over the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' rearranges ERRATIC and SEAT together.
explanation.definitionFit: A secretariat is a body of administrative staff, the collective of office officials.

clue.text: Even those who are long suffering have to be patient here

definitions.text: Even those who are long suffering have to be patient here

parts.words: Even those who are long suffering have to be patient here
parts.note: a place where sufferers, as a doctor's patients, must sit and wait patiently

explanation.surface: Even the most tolerant people need patience somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' doubles as a medical patient, and 'suffering' as being ill.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgery's lounge is where people wait for their appointment.

parts.note: a healer whose patients are literally bound by spells

explanation.surface: A doctor whose patients are captivated by him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spellbound' usually means entranced; here it means treated with spells.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribal healer uses magic and charms to cure the sick.

clue.text: It adds up to the same whichever way you look at it

definitions.text: It adds up to the same whichever way you look at it

parts.words: It adds up to the same whichever way you look at it
parts.note: a grid of numbers whose rows, columns and diagonals all give an equal sum

explanation.surface: Something that is consistent from every angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adds up' sounds figurative, meaning makes sense, but is literal arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: A number grid in which every line totals the same is the recreational-maths puzzle described.

parts.note: pro is short for professional
scribing means writing

explanation.surface: A professional writer is being censored.
explanation.definitionFit: To proscribe is to forbid or outlaw, so the participle means prohibiting.

clue.text: It is no good to dwell over

indicators.note: turned over, the word for dwelling reads backwards

parts.note: to live is to dwell

explanation.surface: Brooding over things does no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses LIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil is wickedness, the opposite of goodness.

clue.text: A beastly place for exchanging lira

indicators.note: exchanging the letters around swaps their places, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A bureau de change for Italian currency is horrid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchanging' rearranges LIRA; the lira was Italy's currency before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild animal's den is the home of a beast.

indicators.note: a cure treats or processes the letters, changing them into a new form

explanation.surface: A miracle cure is being withdrawn from sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cure' rearranges MIRACLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrieve or demand the return of something is to recover it, to summon it home.

definitions.meaning: to be worthy of something, to earn it
the Order of ... is a British honour awarded by the monarch

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to be worthy of reward; as a noun it names the Order of Merit, a British honour.

parts.note: the temperature scale abbreviated to the letter C, not a musical scale in C

explanation.surface: A musical scale in the key of C.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests music; C here is the temperature unit symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Degrees centigrade are abbreviated C, from the centigrade system named after Anders Celsius.

indicators.note: made from the letters, which are rearranged to form the new word

explanation.surface: Words quoted from the official decree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' rearranges EDICT; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite is to quote or refer to a source, so cited means mentioned as a quotation.

clue.text: Back favourite I had found was not so hot

indicators.note: back here means the word for favourite is read backwards

parts.note: a pet is a favourite
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone backed the favourite and found it disappointing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reverses PET to give TEP; 'Back favourite' looks like betting on the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Lukewarm water is only slightly warm, so tepid means less than hot.

parts.note: to do is to act

explanation.surface: Someone takes action amid the fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do is a fuss or stir, a noisy disturbance.

clue.text: Sure turned out to be an employer

indicators.note: turned out suggests the letters are tipped out and reordered

explanation.surface: It turned out the boss was definite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' rearranges SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who employs a thing, putting it to use, is one who uses it.

parts.note: Pip is a short form of Philippa
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Two friends performed together.
explanation.definitionFit: To pipe is to play on a pipe, so piped means played a tune.

parts.note: the hide that wraps a hog all over, which is also leather and an American football

explanation.surface: Something that hides a scoundrel entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swine' tempts as an insult for a person; here it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The hide of a hog wraps its whole body.

clue.text: Mum stirred fluid round, it's as much as the container will hold

definitions.text: as much as the container will hold

indicators.note: the mixed letters go round the call for quiet
stirred means the letters are mixed up

parts.note: mum means silent, and SH is the call for silence

explanation.surface: Mother stirs a liquid in a bowl until it is full.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like Mother, but it means keep quiet, the call for hush.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateful's counterpart for a bowl, the amount a serving vessel holds.

definitions.meaning: to sign someone up for the forces
a newly enlisted member of the army

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to enrol someone into service; as a noun it is a novice serviceman.

clue.text: Interfere with birds mistakenly accepting second person over the channel

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in the other part, holding it inside
mistakenly means the letters are set down in the wrong order

parts.note: tu is French for you, the second person, across the English Channel

explanation.surface: Birds accidentally let a foreigner in and upset things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over the channel' means in France, across the English Channel, so the second person is French.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb something is to meddle with it or disrupt it.

clue.text: Keen giant has lost his head

indicators.note: the giant's name loses its first letter

parts.note: Magog is a legendary giant, paired with Gog

explanation.surface: An eager giant has been beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: GOG and MAGOG are giants of British legend; 'has lost his head' removes the M.
explanation.definitionFit: Being eager and excited is to be on tenterhooks with anticipation.

clue.text: Silly silence before start of argument

parts.note: to gag is to silence

indicators.note: the start of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A foolish hush falls before a row begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Being gaga is being senile or foolishly infatuated.

definitions.meaning: toffee-nosed is British slang for snooty, here the snooty person
an old dialect word for a cobbler

explanation.definitionFit: It means a snooty social climber, and in an older sense a cobbler or shoemaker's apprentice.

clue.text: One hurried to the islands off the west coast Ireland

definitions.text: the islands off the west coast Ireland

parts.note: A is one, the indefinite article
ran means hurried

explanation.surface: A traveller rushed to an Irish island group.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aran Islands lie in Galway Bay on Ireland's Atlantic seaboard.

parts.note: an is the article A

explanation.surface: Help is being sought for a disused train line.
explanation.definitionFit: Charitable gifts to the poor are given for the relief of need.

parts.note: a rank is a grade
to lodge a complaint is to file it

explanation.surface: Assessing and housing the general public.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase originally meant ordinary soldiers and now means the members of a group as opposed to its leaders.

clue.text: Favouring cooking of one's own kind?

definitions.text: Favouring cooking of one's own kind?

parts.words: Favouring cooking of one's own kind?
parts.note: preferring to cook one's own species, not one's own style of food

explanation.surface: A preference for one's own style of cuisine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of one's own kind' looks like a type of cooking but means eating one's own species.
explanation.definitionFit: The practice of eating members of one's own species is the grim sense hidden in the clue.
